devices.name: Device and browser profile inventory
devices.description: A workspace records devices (laptops, PCs, phones, tablets) and the browser profiles on them so their owner knows where accounts are signed in. AkunMu Desktop can read the computer name and the Chrome/Edge/Brave/Vivaldi profiles of the computer it runs on.
devices.purpose: Knowing which devices and browser profiles are used to sign in to the workspace's accounts, as the basis of the sign-in map and security checks.
devices.processing: Recording by hand or from AkunMu Desktop (computer name, browser profile names and folders), showing them on the sign-in map and tree, periodic checks, and deleting and restoring.
devices.legalBasis: Performance of the service agreement with the workspace owner (UU PDP Art. 20(2)(b)). For organization workspaces recording employees' devices: the organization's legitimate interest in account security (Art. 20(2)(f)), with notice to employees.
subjects: Members or employees whose devices are recorded
dataGeneral: Browser profile name, color and folder
devices.source: Entered by workspace members, or read by AkunMu Desktop from the computer it is installed on.
recipientsInternal: Workspace admins and editors (view and edit)
recipientsExternal: AkunMu's infrastructure subprocessors (application hosting and database)
devices.deletion: Devices and profiles can be deleted at any time (trash, then permanently with the workspace). Deleting the workspace deletes the whole inventory.
security: Per-workspace isolation with PostgreSQL row level security (ENABLE + FORCE)
Access limited by role (admin, editor, viewer)
Notes that look like passwords or keys are refused
rights: Access and copy: Settings → My data → Download data (JSON)
Rectification: edit directly in AkunMu
Erasure: delete the device, or delete the workspace in Settings → My data
Other requests: Settings → My data → File a privacy request
flow: Collection: device form or AkunMu Desktop scan
Storage: AkunMu database, isolated per workspace
Use: sign-in map and tree, security checks
End of life: deleted by the user or with the workspace
devices.interests: Workspace owners need to know which devices hold access to their accounts.
devices.necessity: Without the device list the sign-in map cannot show where accounts are signed in.
devices.proportionality: Only name, type and profiles are recorded; no GPS location, IP address or browser content.

location-exposed.event: A device's location or name is seen by unauthorized members
location-exposed.mitigation: Role-based access and RLS; record locations only as needed (e.g. "Office", not a full address).

stale-inventory.event: The device list does not match reality and old sessions are missed
stale-inventory.mitigation: Periodic checks from the extension and desktop; mark devices no longer used.

accounts.name: Online account register
accounts.description: A workspace records accounts on many services (Google, GitHub, Claude and others) with their identifier, two-step verification method and notes. AkunMu never stores passwords or keys.
accounts.purpose: Knowing which accounts exist and on which services, as the basis of the sign-in map and account security.
accounts.processing: Recording accounts, merging the same account seen on several devices and profiles, showing them on the sign-in map and tree, and deleting.
accounts.legalBasis: Performance of the service agreement with the workspace owner (UU PDP Art. 20(2)(b)); for employees' accounts in organization workspaces, the organization's legitimate interest in account security (Art. 20(2)(f)).
subjects: Employees whose work accounts the organization records
dataGeneral: Account identifier: email address or user name
accounts.source: Entered by workspace members, or accepted from browser extension findings.
accounts.deletion: Accounts can be deleted at any time; deletion cascades to the account's sign-ins. Deleting the workspace deletes every account.
security: Passwords, keys and recovery codes are never stored; text that looks like a secret is refused
rights: Access and copy: Download data (JSON) in Settings → My data
Rectification and erasure directly in AkunMu
Other requests: File a privacy request
flow: Collection: account form or accepted extension findings
End of life: deleted by the user or with the workspace
accounts.interests: Owners need a complete picture of their accounts to keep them safe.
accounts.necessity: The identifier is needed to tell accounts on the same service apart.
accounts.proportionality: No passwords, tokens or account contents; only the identifier that also shows on the service's sign-in page.

secret-in-notes.event: A password or key is stored in account notes
secret-in-notes.mitigation: Validation refuses text that looks like a secret; the AI assistant never passes secrets on.

identity-profile.event: The account list forms a full profile of someone's digital identity that could be abused if it leaked
identity-profile.mitigation: Per-workspace RLS, role-based access, time-limited sessions and an audit log.

kept-too-long.mitigation: Review the account list regularly and delete accounts no longer used.

signins.name: Sign-in session map
signins.description: A workspace records on which device and profile each account is signed in, how the session was approved (code, link, QR, confirmation), the session it came from, its status and sign-out history.
signins.purpose: Showing where accounts are signed in so owners can check them and sign out sessions they do not recognize.
signins.processing: Recording sessions (by hand, by the assistant, or from extension findings), automatic confirmation when the extension sees a session again, marking sessions to check, showing them per device and per account, and keeping sign-out history.
signins.legalBasis: Performance of the service agreement (UU PDP Art. 20(2)(b)); for organization workspaces, legitimate interest in account security (Art. 20(2)(f)).
dataGeneral: Account, device and profile or app of the session
Status, start, last verification and sign-out times
signins.source: Workspace members, the AI assistant (after confirmation) and browser extension reports.
signins.deletion: Sessions can be deleted at any time; the history of signed-out sessions is deleted automatically after the retention period in Settings → Privacy.
security: AkunMu stores no cookies or session tokens; only that a session exists
rights: Access and copy: Download data (JSON)
Rectification and erasure directly in AkunMu
Other requests: File a privacy request
flow: Collection: session records or extension findings
End of life: signed out, then deleted after the history retention period
signins.automatedDecision: Sessions the extension sees again are confirmed automatically; sessions on checked sites that are not seen are marked "to check". AkunMu never signs anyone out automatically.
signins.interests: Owners want to know where their accounts are signed in to prevent account takeover.
signins.necessity: The account–device–profile relation is the core of the sign-in map.
signins.proportionality: No session contents, cookies or browsing history; only that a session exists per site.

takeover-map.event: The session map leaks and shows which devices hold access to important accounts
takeover-map.mitigation: RLS, role-based access, time-limited AkunMu sessions and sign-in rate limits.

outdated-status.event: Session statuses are outdated and a foreign session is missed
outdated-status.mitigation: Automatic confirmation from the extension and "to check" markers.

connect.name: Browser extension and AkunMu Desktop
connect.description: The browser extension a user installs checks the names of sign-in cookies on known sites (never their values) to learn where a browser profile is signed in, and reports to AkunMu with a device key. AkunMu Desktop reads the browser profiles of its computer and can open a profile in one click.
connect.purpose: Finding sign-in sessions automatically and keeping the sign-in map up to date without recording by hand.
connect.processing: Creating device keys (only hashes stored), receiving periodic reports (every 6 hours and when the browser opens), creating findings, accepting or ignoring findings by users, and confirming sessions already recorded.
connect.legalBasis: Consent of the user who installs the extension and creates its key (UU PDP Art. 20(2)(a)), and performance of the service agreement (Art. 20(2)(b)). For employees' devices, the organization must inform employees before installing the extension.
subjects: Users of the browser where the extension is installed
Owners of accounts detected in the browser profile
dataGeneral: Account name read from the site page (email or user name)
Device key hash and its last 4 characters
connect.source: The browser extension and AkunMu Desktop on the user's device.
recipientsInternal: Workspace admins and editors (accept or ignore findings)
connect.deletion: Device keys can be revoked at any time; the extension can be removed from the browser; processed findings are deleted automatically after the retention period.
security: The extension only reads cookie names, never cookie values, passwords or keys
Device keys are only stored as SHA-256 hashes
Limit of 120 reports per hour per key
The desktop port listens on 127.0.0.1 only and only forwards reports
rights: Revoke the key or remove the extension at any time (stops the processing)
Access and copy of findings: Download data (JSON)
Erasure of findings directly in AkunMu
flow: Check: the extension in the user's browser
Delivery: HTTPS report with the device key
Processing: new findings or confirmation of recorded sessions
Decision: the user accepts or ignores findings
End of life: findings deleted after the retention period
connect.automatedDecision: Sessions seen again are confirmed automatically; no decision with legal effect.
connect.interests: Users want an up-to-date sign-in map without recording each session.
connect.necessity: Automatic checks keep new sessions from being missed; only domains and account names are sent.
connect.proportionality: The extension is optional, only checks the list of known sites (and other sites when the user asks), and stops when its key is revoked.

token-leak.event: A device key leaks and is used to send fake reports
token-leak.mitigation: Keys are shown once, stored as hashes and revocable; reports are rate limited per hour.

over-collection.event: The extension collects more than needed (cookie values or history)
over-collection.mitigation: The extension code only reads cookie names and account names; the report schema refuses other data.

monitoring-without-notice.event: The extension is installed on employees' devices without notice
monitoring-without-notice.mitigation: Organizations must inform employees and record it in this RoPA before installing the extension.

findings-kept.event: Old findings pile up after processing
findings-kept.mitigation: Set a findings retention period in Settings → Privacy so they are deleted automatically.

assistant.name: AI assistant
assistant.description: Workspace members can ask the AI assistant questions and for actions (for example recording an account or session). The assistant reads data according to role permissions; changes only run after the user approves a confirmation card.
assistant.purpose: Helping manage the sign-in map in everyday language.
assistant.processing: Sending questions and tool results to the AI provider, storing each person's conversation history, and executing approved actions.
assistant.legalBasis: Performance of the service agreement at the user's request (UU PDP Art. 20(2)(b)).
subjects: Owners of accounts and devices the assistant's tools read
dataGeneral: Names of devices, profiles, accounts and sessions in tool results
assistant.source: The user (questions) and workspace data read by tools within their permissions.
recipientsInternal: The user who owns the conversation
recipientsExternal: The AI provider configured by the platform or the workspace (own key)
assistant.deletion: Users can delete their conversations; conversations are deleted automatically after the AI retention period.
security: Secrets are never sent to the AI
Step, time and quota limits per workspace
rights: View and delete conversation history
Choose not to use the assistant (optional feature)
flow: Processing: AI provider with AkunMu tools
assistant.automatedDecision: The AI only proposes actions; nothing changes without the user's approval.
assistant.interests: Users want to manage the sign-in map faster.
assistant.necessity: Tools read only the data needed to answer.
assistant.proportionality: The assistant is optional, quota-limited, and every change needs confirmation.

prompt-abroad.event: Questions and workspace data are sent to an AI provider outside Indonesia
prompt-abroad.mitigation: Choose a provider with a data processing agreement; record the transfer in the RoPA; limit what tools read.

unconfirmed-change.event: The AI changes data without the user knowing
unconfirmed-change.mitigation: All changes go through confirmation cards and are recorded in the audit log.

secret-to-ai.event: A secret (password, key) is sent to the AI
secret-to-ai.mitigation: The assistant refuses secrets; notes that look like secrets are refused before storage.

requests.name: Handling data subject requests
requests.description: Users can file privacy requests (access, rectification, erasure, withdrawal of consent, restriction, objection, portability) to the workspace admins or to the AkunMu operator. Admins can also record requests received by email.
requests.purpose: Fulfilling data subject rights within the deadlines set by UU PDP.
requests.processing: Receiving requests, recording the 3 x 24 hour deadline, handling and answering, and closing.
requests.legalBasis: Compliance with a legal obligation (UU PDP Art. 5–14, 30, 32, 40, 41; PP 33/2026 Art. 76–112).
requests.source: Settings → My data, or recorded by an admin from the requester's email.
recipientsExternal: {processor}: receives requests addressed to the AkunMu operator
requests.retention: As long as needed as proof that the right was fulfilled; can be deleted after closing.
requests.deletion: Closed requests can be deleted by admins; the audit trail remains.
security: Requesters verified by their AkunMu session
Rate limit on requests per user
rights: Requesters see status and answers in Settings → My data
requests.interests: Controllers must fulfil data subject rights on time.
requests.necessity: Only the data needed to identify the requester and the request.
requests.proportionality: Verification uses the existing sign-in session.

missed-deadline.event: A request is not answered within 3 x 24 hours
missed-deadline.mitigation: Deadlines show in the request list and the privacy overview.

impersonation.event: Someone else files a request in the user's name
impersonation.mitigation: In-app requests use the sign-in session; email requests are verified by the admin before acting.

platform-accounts.name: User accounts and authentication
platform-accounts.description: {controller} manages accounts of workspace users and platform staff: account creation, sign-in with email and password, sessions, roles and language.
platform-accounts.purpose: Giving each user secure access to AkunMu according to their role.
platform-accounts.processing: Creating accounts at sign-up or by a workspace admin, storing password hashes, creating sessions, recording the last sign-in time, and deactivating or deleting accounts.
platform-accounts.legalBasis: Performance of the service agreement (UU PDP Art. 20(2)(b)) and legitimate interest in system security (Art. 20(2)(f)).
dataGeneral: Sign-in sessions (token hash, times, browser type)
platform-accounts.source: The user or their workspace admin.
recipientsExternal: AkunMu's infrastructure subprocessors (application hosting and database)
platform-accounts.retention: While the account is active; accounts deleted by their user are anonymized; expired sessions are cleaned up daily.
platform-accounts.deletion: Users delete their account in Settings → My data; admins delete users; platform staff delete workspaces.
security: Session tokens stored only as hashes
rights: Download account data (JSON), correct name and language, delete the account in Settings → My data
Other requests to the operator: File a privacy request
flow: End of life: account deletion and anonymization
platform-accounts.automatedDecision: Temporary automatic lockout after too many sign-in attempts.
platform-accounts.interests: The platform must ensure only authorized people access workspaces.
platform-accounts.necessity: Name, email and password are needed for authentication.
platform-accounts.proportionality: No data beyond what sign-in and roles need.

credential-theft.event: A user's password is stolen and used to sign in
credential-theft.mitigation: bcrypt hashes, sign-in rate limits and time-limited sessions; encourage strong passwords.

stale-accounts.mitigation: Admins review users regularly; users can delete their own account.

platform-signup.name: Workspace sign-up and consent
platform-signup.description: Users sign up for AkunMu by creating a workspace. Acceptance of the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy (required) and product news (optional) are recorded with the policy version as proof.
platform-signup.purpose: Creating the workspace and its first admin, and recording proof of consent.
platform-signup.processing: Collecting workspace and admin details, recording consent and the policy version, and creating the workspace.
platform-signup.legalBasis: Performance of the service agreement (UU PDP Art. 20(2)(b)); consent for product news (Art. 20(2)(a)); proof of consent under PP 33/2026 Art. 36.
dataGeneral: Acceptance of terms and policy with their version
platform-signup.retention: While the account exists; consent records are kept as proof while the account exists.
security: Required consent recorded with the policy version
Product news optional and withdrawable at any time
rights: Withdraw product news consent in Settings → My data
View consent records in Settings → My data
flow: Consent: recorded with the policy version
platform-signup.interests: The platform needs to know who created a workspace and that they accepted the terms.
platform-signup.necessity: Only the workspace and admin details needed to create the account.
platform-signup.proportionality: Product news is separate and optional.

marketing-without-consent.event: A user is contacted with product news without consent
marketing-without-consent.mitigation: Product news only for those who ticked it; the choice is recorded and withdrawable.

fake-signup.event: Fake sign-ups or sign-ups in someone else's name
fake-signup.mitigation: Rate limit per IP and review of workspaces by platform staff.

platform-security.name: Audit log and abuse protection
platform-security.description: {controller} records who did what (audit log) and limits repeated attempts (sign-in, sign-up, extension reports) for security and accountability.
platform-security.purpose: Keeping the system secure, investigating incidents, and proving data protection compliance.
platform-security.processing: Recording user and system actions with their subjects, and attempt counters per email, IP address or device key in short time windows.
platform-security.legalBasis: Legitimate interest in system security and accountability obligations (UU PDP Art. 20(2)(c) and (f); Art. 35).
subjects: Visitors attempting to sign in or sign up
dataGeneral: IP address and email in attempt-limit keys (temporary)
platform-security.deletion: Expired attempt counters are deleted automatically; audit logs are deleted after the retention period.
security: Attempt counters in the shared database
rights: Access to log entries about a person through a privacy request to the operator
flow: Recording: automatically when an action happens
platform-security.automatedDecision: Automatic temporary block when an attempt limit is exceeded.
platform-security.necessity: Logs record object numbers, not copies of personal data; IP addresses are only kept temporarily.
platform-security.proportionality: Attempt counters expire within minutes to hours.

log-overcollection.event: Logs keep more personal data than needed
log-overcollection.mitigation: Logs keep only object numbers and brief metadata.

log-kept-forever.event: Logs and attempt counters are never deleted
log-kept-forever.mitigation: Automatic retention: expired counters are purged daily; the audit log retention is set in platform Settings.

platform-ai.name: AI gateway and quota metering
platform-ai.description: {controller} provides AI for the assistant through AI providers configured by the platform or the workspace's own key, and counts usage per workspace for quotas.
platform-ai.purpose: Providing AI features and limiting usage according to the plan.
platform-ai.processing: Forwarding AI requests to providers, storing the model's thinking blocks to continue conversations, and monthly usage counters per workspace.
platform-ai.legalBasis: Performance of the service agreement (UU PDP Art. 20(2)(b)).
subjects: People mentioned in text processed by AI
dataGeneral: Requests and tokens per workspace per month
platform-ai.deletion: Conversations are deleted by users or automatically after the AI retention period; usage figures are kept for quotas.
security: API keys stored encrypted and never sent to the browser
rights: Users can delete their conversations
platform-ai.interests: Offering safe AI features with controlled costs.
platform-ai.necessity: Only the text needed for the AI task is sent.
platform-ai.proportionality: Usage counters are aggregate figures, not content.

provider-retention.event: The AI provider keeps or uses data for other purposes
provider-retention.mitigation: Choose providers whose API terms do not train models on customer data; review their agreement.

transfer-abroad.event: Data is sent to an AI provider outside Indonesia without equivalent protection
transfer-abroad.mitigation: Record the transfer in the RoPA, assess the destination's level of protection, and use a data processing agreement.
